biological.citation: Chronic stress induces depression through MDGA1-Neuroligin2 mediated suppression of inhibitory synapses in the lateral habenula (PMID: 39897557)
biological.summary: NLGN2 selectively interacts with MDGA1 in the lateral habenula. MDGA1-mediated suppression of NLGN2 limits GABAergic synapse formation and facilitates depression onset. Introduction of NLGN2 variant incapable of binding MDGA1 enhanced inhibitory transmission and increased GABAergic synapse density, conferring resistance to stress-induced depression.

biological.citation: Identifying therapeutic target genes for migraine by systematic druggable genome-wide Mendelian randomization (PMID: 38867170)
biological.summary: NLGN2 was identified as one of 21 druggable genes significantly associated with migraine through genome-wide Mendelian randomization analysis using brain and blood eQTLs and GWAS data.

biological.citation: NLGN1 and NLGN2 in the prefrontal cortex: their role in memory consolidation and strengthening (PMID: 29278843)
biological.summary: NLGN2 is an inhibitory synaptic protein in the prefrontal cortex that regulates memory formation and modulation of memory strength. Changes in NLGN2 expression in inhibitory neuronal subpopulations regulate dynamic processes of memory consolidation and strengthening.

biological.citation: Large-scale discovery of novel neurodevelopmental disorder-related genes through a unified analysis of single-nucleotide and copy number variants (PMID: 35468861)
biological.summary: NLGN2 was identified as a high-confidence (>90% true-positive probability) candidate gene for neurodevelopmental disorders through integrated analysis of de novo SNVs and CNVs in 41,165 individuals with NDDs, based on functional similarity to known NDD genes.

biological.citation: Functional Neuroligin-2-MDGA1 interactions differentially regulate synaptic GABA(A)Rs and cytosolic gephyrin aggregation (PMID: 39284869)
biological.summary: NLGN2 recruits GABAARs by promoting assembly of the postsynaptic gephyrin scaffold. Loss of MDGA1, but not MDGA2, ameliorates abnormal cytosolic gephyrin aggregation and reduction in inhibitory synaptic transmission in NLGN2 knockout mice, indicating MDGA1 modulates NLGN2 function at GABAergic synapses.

biological.citation: Licochalcone A prevents cognitive decline in a lipopolysaccharide-induced neuroinflammation mice model (PMID: 39930360)
biological.summary: NLGN2 mRNA expression was significantly reduced in the brains of LPS-treated mice compared to saline controls, and this reduction was associated with memory impairment and depressive-like behavior. LCA treatment protected against LPS-induced downregulation of NLGN2 and other synaptic proteins.

biological.citation: GluN2D Subunit in Parvalbumin Interneurons Regulates Prefrontal Cortex Feedforward Inhibitory Circuit and Molecular Networks Relevant to Schizophrenia (PMID: 37004850)
biological.summary: NLGN2 is involved in formation of inhibitory synapses and was downregulated in PV-GluN2D knockout mice. NLGN2 is part of molecular networks regulating GABAergic synapses and is associated with schizophrenia susceptibility genes.

biological.citation: Expression and structural analysis of human neuroligin 2 and neuroligin 3 implicated in autism spectrum disorders (PMID: 36479216)
biological.summary: NLGN2 and NLGN3 have distinct distributions and functions in synapse development and plasticity. Cryo-EM structures reveal relative rotations of NLGN2 homodimers that may affect interactions with MDGAs, suggesting distinct assembly mechanisms that could affect their roles in autism spectrum disorder development.
biological.sample_size: streptozotocin-induced ASD mouse model; structural analysis of human NLGN2

biological.citation: Distinct mechanisms control the specific synaptic functions of Neuroligin 1 and Neuroligin 2 (PMID: 39747663)
biological.summary: NLGN2 selectively functions in inhibitory synapses and restores inhibitory synaptic transmission in neuroligin-deficient neurons. The extracellular domains of NLGN2 confer inhibitory synapse specificity, while its cytoplasmic sequences including the Gephyrin-binding motif are essential for synaptic function.

biological.citation: ASHG 2018 - Targeted sequencing of postsynaptic protein genes associated with schizophrenia: A role for multiple rare risk mutations in schizophrenia susceptibility (M. Cheng et al.)
biological.summary: A rare missense mutation NLGN2 p.R309Q was identified in schizophrenia patients but absent in 1,517 healthy controls and ExAC database. Immunoblot analysis showed this mutation decreased NLGN2 protein expression in HEK293 cells compared to wild-type, suggesting loss-of-function contribution to schizophrenia.
